startup.name: Constellation Space
startup.one_liner: AI operating system for mega scale satellite networks
startup.description: Software layer for operating very large satellite constellations: automated network handoffs, thermal load balancing and optical link routing. Sold to constellation operators. Four founders from SpaceX, Blue Origin and NASA. Batch Winter 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test note: the company was accepted, so this is an if accepted view. A blind prior starts near 1 percent, and the factors in the YC acceptance table are applied loosely here. Not part of the scored test.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC might decline because the pitch is full of buzzwords with no named customer or demo, the buyer set is a few dozen operators, and the biggest constellation, Starlink, already runs its own routing in house. Interviewers may doubt that outsiders can sell core network software to operators.

anchors.source: Ran python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only: seed 49 / 59 / 65 percent (lower, known, upper), series A 13 / 15 / 29 with cond 26 percent (n=74), series B cond 16 percent (n=19), series C cond 0 percent (n=3, too small). Broad cohort also checked with --industry B2B --years 2018-2021: seed cond 81, A cond 32, B cond 39, C cond 57 percent.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Set a bit below the 59 percent anchor because the buyers are few and sales cycles are long, offset by active space seed funding for founders from SpaceX and Blue Origin (basil and cascade analogs raised seeds). The seed step here means a round above the standard 500K YC deal within about 12 months, and the anchor is for any seed ever, so the 12 month window pulls it down while a hot category pushes it up.

bands.rationale: Small round just above the YC check, mostly angels, if traction is thin.

ladder.why_it_fails: A round above the YC check fails if there is no signed pilot with an operator. Space software investors want a named customer, and operators protect their routing stack. Analogs like quindar sold to ground operations teams only after years of customer proofs, and a pre revenue pitch may be seen as a slide deck.

bands.rationale: Standard Series C near the 2022+ median of about 45M to 80M raise for researched companies.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C fails if the company stays a niche tool with a handful of customers. A defense or telecom acquirer may buy it earlier than a large round. The total addressable market for constellation software is small compared with ground network or cloud markets. The same pattern showed up for quindar, where customer proof for satellite operators took years, and for spaceryde, which ran out of runway before commercial revenue.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely failure is a thin customer base: a handful of operators buy core software slowly or build it themselves, so revenue never justifies a large round. Space software tends to end in small acquisitions by larger primes, and the claims on the YC page are untested.

killers.risk: Few buyers and in house stacks at the biggest operators
killers.evidence: Starlink already uses neural network traffic prediction and its own optimizer, and other large operators build ground software themselves.
killers.mitigation: Target mid sized and new constellation operators, and sell as a pilot with measurable link efficiency.

killers.risk: Unproven technical claims such as zero intervention handoffs and sub second optical routing
killers.evidence: The YC text lists capabilities with no demo, customer or test data.
killers.mitigation: Publish simulation results and run a live pilot with a partner.

killers.risk: Slow sales and government cycles starve the company
killers.evidence: Trade sources say autonomy shifts in ground segments will be incremental.
killers.mitigation: Win small paid pilots and SBIR style funding.

killers.risk: Competing software defined ground segment vendors
killers.evidence: Leanspace, Cognitive Space and Slingshot sell related platforms. according to the market research gathered for this evaluation and the analog records.
killers.mitigation: Focus on optical routing, an area few address.

competition_now.name: Starlink in house routing
competition_now.what: Neural network traffic prediction with optimizer for beams and crosslinks.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous routing, thermal balancing and optical link scheduling at tens of thousands of nodes is hard, needs operator data and simulation, and cannot be validated without a real constellation. A four person team can build simulations and a pilot but not prove scale quickly.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents with ground segment software could add routing in about two years, and big operators already do it internally. Smaller constellation operators lack that ability, which is the opening, but platform owners may also acquire.

evidence.claim: Optical inter satellite links and autonomous operations are growing priorities, with AI in space operations projected to grow about 23 percent a year by one trade analysis.
European operators and others are scaling optical connectivity.

roadmap.goal: Scale to mid sized operators and defense.

narrative.headline: Strong pedigree on a hard technical problem with very few buyers, so a seed is possible but later rounds depend on a named operator customer.
narrative.general_summary: Constellation Space sells network operations software for giant satellite constellations. The founders have relevant backgrounds and space software has raised money, as quindar and basalt show. But the buyer set is tiny, the largest operator builds its own system, and the YC text lists capabilities with no customers. A seed above the YC check is a coin flip within a year, and later rounds depend on converting pilots to recurring contracts. Space cases in the data include both a shutdown after a long hardware path and a firm that reached a Series A.
